data.body:
PROGRESS (2026-07-24) — boundary coverage + help; MCP split out.

Scope: MCP removed from this epic (description + file_impact updated). The MCP `review_plan`
sign opt-out and its machine-readable unsigned reason are split to 2cd3-062b-f99d-4143
(weedy-distant-asp), linked discovered_from.

Landed for review as Gerrit change 961 (commit 98feaf2, worktree 58f2-plan-review-sign-boundary):
- parser-boundary tests: omitting `--no-sign` reaches the library as sign=True; the flag is the
  only CLI route to an unsigned review.
- library contract tests: sign=True default persists a CLAIM-VALID attestation on the ticket;
  sign=False withholds it and the claim is blocked (exit 1, ticket stays open).
- end-to-end over the REAL CLI route: `rebar review-plan <id>` signs, and the subsequent
  `rebar claim` is satisfied with NO second LLM call.
- never-sign guard table: BLOCK, not-claimable INDETERMINATE, explicit sign=False.
- idempotent reuse emits no SECOND signature (signed_at unmoved) — the gap the existing
  short-circuit test left.
- `--no-sign` help now STATES the sign-by-default contract and names `sign-review` as the
  no-LLM recovery; a drift test pins the text.
Verified: make lint, make typecheck, full non-integration suite (4038 passed, 0 failures).

DISCOVERED, blocking AC5: `review-plan --source local` signs a claim-valid attestation with
verified_at_sha=None, though the CLI help says local "never signs" — filed as
5128-0856-d80f-4eb6 (melancholy-firstborn-shihtzu), linked discovered_from. AC5's local-source
and exempt clauses assert behavior that does not hold today, so they are deliberately NOT
pinned here; pinning them would encode the bypass as expected.

Also note AC1/AC2/AC8 referenced an "affected `rebar review` plan route". No such route exists:
`rebar review` is the separate `review_ticket` op (_cli/__init__.py:413), not a plan-review
surface. The e2e was written against the real `review-plan` CLI route instead.
